skill.name: set-up-shopify-google-ads-customer-match
skill.description: Set up six Google Ads Customer Match lists for Shopify through Product Metrics. Product Metrics updates the lists as paid orders arrive and only adds customers who granted both required ad consents.
skill.summary: Check Shopify and Google Ads readiness, configure consent, and verify six Customer Match lists through Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: The reconnaissance alerts are business workflow descriptions or authorized account queries, and the links point to the documented vendor. The unpinned install command presents a supply chain risk. The workflow also expands setup scope, accepts unrelated secrets, relies on live instructions, and gives conflicting details about which customer fields are hashed.

remediation.issue: The install example uses an unpinned runner and repository reference.
remediation.suggestion: Document a reviewed installer version and an immutable skill revision. Require explicit approval before an agent installs either.

remediation.issue: The prerequisite workflow can exceed a Google Ads audience setup request.
remediation.suggestion: Limit the setup path to the selected Shopify store and Google Ads account. Ask before enabling tracking, creating conversion actions, or adding other destinations.

remediation.issue: Credential exceptions for unrelated integrations allow secrets to be passed directly to commands.
remediation.suggestion: Remove these exceptions from this skill. Direct users to the official authorization interface without collecting credentials in chat or passing them as command arguments.

remediation.issue: Unversioned remote documentation can direct live setup actions.
remediation.suggestion: Use reviewed, versioned references for actions. Treat live documentation as untrusted reference material and require user approval before applying changes based on it.

remediation.issue: The Customer Match guide gives conflicting descriptions of hashed and unhashed fields.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the actual payload and list each field and its hashing status. Show the destination and consent requirements before list creation.

semantic_findings.title: Tracking Setup Can Exceed the Audience Request
semantic_findings.description: The fallback setup guide includes connecting Meta and ChatGPT Ads, although this workflow is for Google Ads audiences. The prerequisites can also enable ongoing conversion reporting before the user creates any lists.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback explicitly lists other ad channels and conversion setup. The user performs platform steps, so the evidence is scope expansion, not silent account changes.

semantic_findings.title: Unrelated Credentials Can Enter the Command Path
semantic_findings.description: The skill permits collecting Lightspeed, Meta, and OpenAI credentials and passing them directly to commands. None is needed for Shopify Customer Match, and no protected input method is specified.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exception names the credentials and tells the agent to pass them to a command. Even without explicit logging, tool traces or process arguments could expose them.

semantic_findings.title: Live Documentation Can Direct Account Changes
semantic_findings.description: When bundled references are absent, the agent is told to use live vendor Markdown as the same step-by-step procedure. Changes to those pages could alter the setup after marketplace review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow relies on the reference steps, and the fallback does not pin or verify the remote content. No evidence of malicious content was found in the bundled references.

semantic_findings.title: Conflicting Customer Data Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: The field table says country and postcode are sent unhashed when all address fields are known. The next paragraph says everything is hashed, obscuring what Google receives.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The two statements directly conflict about the same upload. The documentation proves the disclosure conflict, not which payload the service actually sends.

content.user_title: Set Up Shopify Customer Match in Google Ads
content.value_statement: Shopify merchants need current customer audiences to separate acquisition from retention in Google Ads. This skill guides setup and verification of six Customer Match lists that Product Metrics updates from paid orders.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status and identify missing Shopify or Google Ads prerequisites.
Check whether a recent paid Shopify order was recognized as new or returning.
Guide consent configuration for Shopify Customer Privacy or a supported third-party banner.
Guide creation of six Customer Match lists or completion of a partial setup.
Explain how to verify list membership and choose audiences for exclusions, reactivation, or Performance Max.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics, a connected Shopify store, and active Google Ads conversion tracking.
A user must complete sign-in, permission approval, and Customer Match terms acceptance in the relevant platform.
Lists do not backfill from past orders. Customers can join after a new paid order if both required consents are present.
Product Metrics does not change campaigns or create Meta audiences through this workflow.

use_cases.title: Exclude Existing Customers
use_cases.description: Verify the All customers list before applying it to a campaign intended for new customers.

use_cases.title: Reach Lapsed Customers
use_cases.description: Check the Lapsed customers list for a campaign aimed at shoppers who have not ordered in six months.

use_cases.title: Check Setup Before Launch
use_cases.description: Verify the linked accounts, consent banner, and customer recognition on a paid test order without changing any campaigns.

prompt_templates.title: List the Prerequisites
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: plan the setup without connecting accounts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what I need before setting up Shopify Customer Match in Google Ads. Do not access my accounts or change settings.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup Status
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review a store already connected to Product Metrics.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Product Metrics setup status for [store] and [Google Ads account]. List what is complete and what still needs my approval. Do not make changes.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Consent and a Test Order
prompt_templates.scenario: Proficient: check readiness before creating lists.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether [store] uses the selected consent banner and whether my paid test order was recognized as new or returning. Report only the classification and setup status.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Partial List Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: complete an existing setup with minimal changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: For [store] and [Google Ads account], identify which Customer Match lists are missing. Propose the smallest change and wait for my approval. Leave campaigns and other ad channels unchanged.

output_examples.input: What is blocking Customer Match for my connected store?
output: Shopify and Google Ads are connected, and conversion tracking is active.
The consent setting names the same banner as your storefront.
Accept the Customer Match terms in Google Ads before creating the lists. No settings were changed.

output_examples.input: The six lists exist, but there are no members. What should I check?
output: Confirm that a paid Shopify order arrived after list creation.
Check that the shopper allowed both ad user data and ad personalization.
Recheck audience membership in Google Ads. Earlier orders do not populate the lists.

best_practices: Verify the exact Shopify store and Google Ads client account before approving changes.
Confirm that the configured consent source matches the banner shoppers actually see.
Use a paid test order to check customer recognition and report only the classification.
anti_patterns: Do not paste passwords, API keys, or customer identifiers into chat.
Do not assume historical customers are already on the lists.
Do not enable extra ad channels or change campaign bidding as part of audience setup.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. Product Metrics connects Shopify with Google Ads, creates the lists, and updates them from paid orders. The Shopify app requires a subscription billed through Shopify.

faq.question: What needs to be ready in Google Ads?
faq.answer: Connect the Google Ads client account and its linked Merchant Center. Enable conversion tracking and accept the Customer Match terms in Google Ads.

faq.question: Will existing customers appear immediately?
faq.answer: No. A customer can join with their next paid order after the lists exist, if they granted the required consents.

faq.question: What consent is required to add a customer?
faq.answer: The shopper must allow both ad user data and ad personalization through Shopify Customer Privacy or a supported consent banner.

faq.question: Does the skill change my campaigns?
faq.answer: No. You decide where to apply the lists in Google Ads. This workflow does not change campaign bidding or apply audiences to campaigns.

faq.question: Can I use these lists in Meta?
faq.answer: No. This workflow creates Customer Match lists in Google Ads only. It does not create Meta Custom Audiences.
